name: Pinyin
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Pinyin (Grassfields, Cameroon): only SIL sociolinguistic surveys (Ayotte & Lamberty 2003; Brye 2005; Kruger 2004) on Glottolog; no phonology found; tonal language.

sources.citation: Sadembouo, Etienne & Sue Hasselbring. 1991. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Ngemba Languages. Yaounde: SIL. 31 pp. (image-only scan)
sources.note: Only the title page was viewed (no text layer, not scanned); it is a sociolinguistic survey, not a phonological description.

sources.citation: Mbah, Njeck Mathaus & Stephen C. Anderson. 2005. The Pinyin Orthography Guide. Yaounde: CABTAL / SIL Cameroon (November 2005 revision), 14 pp. [source of PHOIBLE inventory GM 1632]
sources.note: Nothing. Sections 2 (Alphabet: 25 consonants, 8 vowels, long vowels, diphthongs) and 3 (Tone, pp. 7-8: 'We have identified five surface tones in Pinyin: three level tones, high, mid and low; and two contour tones, rising and falling'; low tone unmarked in orthography; words written in isolation forms) contain no statement about stress, accent or prominence. The text layer uses a shifted font encoding; a is saved alongside.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Pinyin language' — phonology section derived from Mbah & Anderson 2005.
sources.note: Consonants, vowels, five tones; nothing on stress. Supplied the silcam.org URL for the orthography guide.

sources.citation: Watters, John R. 2003. Grassfields Bantu. In Nurse & Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages, ch. 14. London: Routledge. (text already on file)
sources.note: Mentions Pinyin only in the Ngemba classification list (16,000 speakers 1982); no Pinyin-specific prosodic statement and no stress statement in the vicinity.

sources.citation: Ayotte, Michael & Melinda Lamberty. 2002/2003. Rapid Appraisal Sociolinguistic Survey among the Ngemba Cluster of Languages: Mankon, Bambili, Nkwen, Pinyin, and Awing. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2003-002.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey (intelligibility, attitudes). Its reference list adds no Pinyin phonology beyond Leroy 1980 (noun classes) and the SIL surveys.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0 inventory GM 1632 'Pinyin' (contributed by C. Green & S. Moran), citing Mbah & Anderson 2005.
sources.note: Segment and tone inventory only (H, M, L, HL fall, LH rise); no stress information.
